Replace GPG signing with Sigstore/cosign keyless signing:

Signatures prove artifacts were built by GitHub Actions in this repo

feat(agents): enable streaming responses with tool support

Previously, when tools were enabled the LLM response arrived all at once
after processing completed because the code used the non-streaming
`complete()` method. This change enables real-time token streaming even
when tools are available.

Changes:
- Extend StreamEvent enum with ToolCallStart, ToolCallArgumentsDelta,
  and ToolCallComplete variants for streaming tool calls
- Add stream_with_tools() method to LlmProvider trait with default
  fallback to stream()
- Implement streaming with tools in AnthropicProvider, handling
  content_block_start/delta/stop events for tool_use blocks
- Add run_agent_loop_streaming() that uses streaming API and emits
  TextDelta events as text arrives while accumulating tool calls
- Update gateway to use the new streaming agent loop

The UI now receives text tokens in real-time via WebSocket delta events,
providing a much better user experience when using Anthropic models with
tools enabled.

fix(migrations): use set_ignore_missing to allow multi-crate migrations

Each crate's migrations are tracked in the shared _sqlx_migrations table.
When running migrations from one crate, SQLx would error if it found
migrations from other crates in the table. Using set_ignore_missing(true)
allows each migrator to ignore migrations it doesn't own.

Also add integration tests for migrations using temp directories.

feat(chat): add Prompt button to inspect full system prompt

Add a chat.raw_prompt RPC method and a "Prompt" toolbar button that
displays the complete system prompt sent to the model, including
character count, tool count, and native_tools flag.

Also removes the redundant "Current Session" section from the prompt
(message count and token stats) since the LLM already sees the full
conversation history. The session name is retained in the Runtime

fix(sandbox): create /home/sandbox directory in generated images

Apple Container maps processes to a sandbox user with

images. Add mkdir, ENV HOME, and WORKDIR to the Dockerfile template.

fix(sandbox): create /home/sandbox at container startup via exec

The Dockerfile-based approach doesn't reliably work with Apple

run mkdir -p /home/sandbox via exec right after container creation
in both Docker and Apple Container backends.

fix(sandbox): default working directory to /home/sandbox

Change the sandbox default working directory from / to /home/sandbox

Remove leading whitespace from Dockerfile instruction lines in all

Stop removing /var/lib/apt/lists/* after package installation in

but it broke apt install inside running containers — users had to

fix(tools): handle empty session_name in process tool start action

LLMs often send all fields with empty defaults ("session_name": "")
rather than omitting optional ones. The start action now treats empty
strings as absent and auto-generates a session name, instead of
rejecting them with an invalid session_name error.

fix(gateway): validate config before restart to prevent crash loops

The /api/restart endpoint now reads and parses the saved config from disk
before restarting. If the TOML is invalid or unreadable, it returns an
error instead of restarting — preventing the server from crashing on
startup. The frontend handles the error response and displays it to the
user instead of entering the reconnection polling loop.

fix(gateway): use YAML list for allowed-tools in seeded tmux skill

The TMUX_SKILL_MD constant used a scalar string for allowed-tools
which fails serde deserialization into Vec<String>. Changed to a
proper YAML list so the skill parses correctly on first seed.

feat(gateway): voice pending UI, TTS phrase generation, and empty message filtering

Add voice_pending broadcast and UI indicator so the frontend suppresses
streaming deltas while server-side TTS is generating, then renders the
final audio player and transcript together.

Filter empty assistant messages from session history responses
(resolve, preview, chat.history) so they are not shown in the web UI
or sent to channels, while keeping them in JSONL storage for LLM
history coherence. Also clean up lingering stream elements and fall
back to the last exec card for model/token footer on silent replies.

Add TTS phrase generation module and JS integration for natural
voice responses.

feat(gateway): persist TTS audio, per-session media, and silent replies

- Persist TTS audio to session media directory so voice responses
  survive page reload without re-generating via RPC
- Add per-session media directory (sessions/media/<key>/) with
  cleanup on session delete and media serving API endpoint
- Suppress streaming text when voice response is pending, showing
  a "Generating voice response" indicator instead, then rendering
  audio widget above transcript text on completion
- Filter empty assistant messages from persistence and suppress
  empty chat bubbles, push notifications, and channel replies
- Extract shared helpers (renderAudioPlayer, renderScreenshot,
  toolCallSummary) to helpers.js and reuse across websocket/sessions
- Add TTS phrase generation with LLM-powered natural language
  conversion for voice responses
- Support audio field in session history for both live and
  history rendering paths

fix(gateway): auto-enable ElevenLabs counterpart in onboarding voice test

When testing an ElevenLabs provider for one type (e.g. STT), also enable
the counterpart type (TTS) since they share the same API key.

fix(gateway): persist empty assistant messages for LLM history coherence

Remove the `is_empty()` guard from both send() and send_sync() persistence
paths. Empty assistant messages (after tool-only responses) must be stored
so the LLM sees proper user→assistant turn alternation. Without this,
consecutive user messages cause the LLM to re-execute earlier commands.
The UI-side filter_ui_history() already hides empty messages from clients.

fix(gateway): remove separate voice-generating indicator during TTS

Keep the classic thinking dots visible throughout the entire response
cycle instead of swapping to a "Generating voice response…" indicator
when TTS begins. This avoids showing two sequential thinking states.

fix(gateway): enable TTS counterpart when saving ElevenLabs/Google STT key

The save_key handler for "elevenlabs-stt" and "google" STT saved the API
key to both STT and TTS config (shared key) but only enabled the STT
provider. The TTS counterpart handlers ("elevenlabs", "google-tts")
already enabled both directions — this makes the STT handlers symmetric.

Also fix the frontend onboarding where provider ID mismatch ("elevenlabs"
vs "elevenlabs-stt") caused the counterpart toggle and onSaveKey toggle
calls to silently fail. A COUNTERPART_IDS mapping now resolves the correct
ID for each direction.

feat(gateway): add Context button showing full LLM messages array

Add a "Context" button next to Debug and Prompt that displays the
complete messages array sent to the LLM — system prompt + conversation
history — as a structured, human-readable view with collapsible
per-message sections, color-coded role badges, tool call formatting,
and auto-refresh on user send and LLM response completion.

fix(gateway): reconstruct tool messages in full context view

Convert persisted tool_result entries into role:"tool" messages when
building the full context, so the Context panel shows the exec output
the LLM actually saw during the agent loop.

feat(gateway): add queued message UI with cancel support

Show queued (pending) messages with a distinct visual style (dashed
border, reduced opacity, "Queued" badge) and a cancel button so the
user knows which messages are waiting and can remove them before they
reach the LLM.

- Add cancel_queued method to ChatService trait and LiveChatService
- Register chat.cancel_queued RPC in WRITE_METHODS
- Include queue position in existing queued broadcast
- Frontend: mark user messages as queued on sendRpc response, add
  markMessageQueued with cancel button calling chat.cancel_queued
- WebSocket: handle queue_cleared event (remove queued elements),
  clear queued styling on first queued message when thinking starts
- CSS: .msg.user.queued, .queued-badge, .queued-cancel styles
- Add 3 unit tests for cancel_queued logic

fix(gateway): fix queued message detection and ordering

The queued check was reading res?.queued but the RPC response frame
wraps the payload: { ok, payload: { queued: true } }. Fixed to check
res?.payload?.queued so the queued styling actually gets applied.

Also move the first queued user message to the bottom of the chat when
thinking starts, so user→assistant ordering is preserved. Without this,
sending 3 messages while the LLM is busy would show all 3 user messages
stacked together followed by all 3 LLM responses.

fix(gateway): move queued messages to dedicated bottom tray

Queued messages now live in a separate container pinned between the
chat area and the input box, visually distinct from the conversation.
This prevents the broken ordering where 3 user messages would stack
then 3 LLM responses follow.

- Add #queuedMessages tray to chat grid layout (new row)
- markMessageQueued moves the element from the chat into the tray
- handleChatThinking moves the first tray item back into the chat
  flow right before the thinking indicator (correct ordering)
- handleChatQueueCleared empties and hides the tray
- Add .queued-tray CSS with dashed top border and surface background

fix(gateway): clear queued tray on session switch and add debug logs

The queued messages tray was not cleared when switching sessions or on
WebSocket reconnect, causing stale queued messages to reappear. Now
switchSession() empties and hides the tray.

Added console.debug logs at key queued message lifecycle points
(mark, thinking-move, clear) and an info! log in cancel_queued to
help trace ordering issues.

fix(gateway): never attach model footer or timestamp to user messages

The silent-reply fallback in handleChatFinal picked
chatMsgBox.lastElementChild which could be a user message (especially
after a queued message is moved from the tray). Now both
appendFinalFooter and appendLastMessageTimestamp skip elements with
the .user class.

fix(gateway): prevent multi-move race in queued message tray

Extract moveFirstQueuedToChat() with a data-moving flag on the tray
element so that only the first thinking event per LLM run moves a
message from the queue. Multi-iteration runs (tool calls) fire
multiple thinking events; without the flag each one moved a separate
queued message, causing batched responses.

The flag is cleared by handleChatFinal at the end of each run,
readying the tray for the next queued message.

fix(gateway): defer user message persist until after semaphore

Previously, send() persisted the user message to the session store
before checking the per-session semaphore. When the semaphore was
held, the message was queued and returned early — but it had already
been written to the JSONL file. When the queue later replayed the
message via send(), it was persisted a second time, causing
duplicates in the LLM context and duplicate UI renders.

Move the persist call to after the semaphore is acquired. Queued
messages are now only persisted when they actually run. The history
read no longer needs to pop the last entry since the user message
hasn't been appended yet (run_streaming / run_agent_loop append it
themselves).

feat(gateway): add Copy button to full context panel

Adds a "Copy" button next to the message stats in the full context
panel. Clicking it copies all messages as a readable text dump
([role] content) to the clipboard for easy pasting when debugging.

fix(gateway): move queued messages only after response is rendered

Previously, moveFirstQueuedToChat() was called during the thinking
event, which caused the next queued user message to appear in the
chat BEFORE the current response finished rendering. With
multi-iteration runs (tool calls), this resulted in wrong ordering:
user-msg → next-user-msg → exec-card instead of user-msg →
exec-card → next-user-msg.

Now queued messages are moved from the tray at the END of
handleChatFinal (after all response content is rendered) and in
handleChatError. This gives correct ordering: each user message
appears right before its corresponding response.

Also removes the data-moving flag machinery which is no longer
needed since thinking events no longer move tray messages.

feat(gateway): add client-side message sequence number for ordering diagnostics

JS assigns an auto-incrementing _seq to every chat.send RPC call.
The server tracks the last-seen seq per session and logs warnings
when it detects duplicates, reordering, or gaps. Seq resets to 1
on page reload are handled gracefully (no false warnings).

This provides observability for message ordering issues without
enforcing anything yet — the warnings appear in server logs to help
debug race conditions.

feat(gateway): add run_id and seq to persisted messages for parent/child linking

Wire sequence numbers and run IDs through the full message lifecycle:
- Add run_id field to PersistedMessage::User and Assistant variants,
  linking each user message to the agent run that processes it
- Persist client_seq on both user and assistant messages in JSONL
- Include seq in all chat broadcasts (thinking, tool, final, error)
  via the event callback closure
- Generate run_id before user message construction so it can be
  stored on the user message at persist time
- Move chatSeq to shared state (state.js) and resume from the
  highest user seq in history on session switch, preventing
  counter resets on page reload

refactor(gateway): use typed structs for chat broadcast payloads

Replace serde_json::json! post-hoc mutation of seq/run_id with:
- ChatFinalBroadcast struct for "final" events (compile-time safety)
- ChatErrorBroadcast struct for "error" events
- Direct "seq" inclusion in all event callback json! macros
  instead of post-hoc payload["seq"] = ... mutation

This follows the CLAUDE.md rule to use concrete Rust types instead
of serde_json::Value wherever the shape is known.

feat(channels): add reply threading support for Telegram messages

Add message_id to ChannelReplyTarget so outbound replies can thread
as responses to the user's original message. The ChannelOutbound trait
now accepts an optional reply_to parameter on send_text, send_media,
and send_text_silent. TelegramOutbound uses Telegram's ReplyParameters
API to thread the first chunk of each reply.

fix(tools): fall back to DuckDuckGo when web_search API key is missing

When no Brave or Perplexity API key is configured, the web_search tool
now transparently falls back to DuckDuckGo HTML search instead of
returning an error that forces the LLM to ask the user about opening a
browser.

The fallback POSTs to html.duckduckgo.com/html/, parses the result HTML
with lightweight string matching, resolves DDG redirect URLs via the
`uddg` query parameter, and returns results in the same JSON format as
the primary providers. If DuckDuckGo also fails (CAPTCHA, network
error), the original provider error is returned for graceful degradation.

Includes formatting changes from cargo fmt on channel/telegram files.

fix(onboarding): skip finish screen and redirect to chat directly

Remove the intermediate "You're all set!" step from the onboarding
wizard. When completing the last step, users are now redirected
straight to the chat page — one less click.

fix(ui): rename Images nav item to Sandboxes

"Sandboxes" communicates the feature to users better than the
implementation-detail label "Images".

refactor(ui): rename /images and /api/images routes to /sandboxes

Update the page route from /images to /sandboxes and all API endpoints
from /api/images/* to /api/sandboxes/* to match the nav rename.

fix(ui): revert API routes to /api/images, remove "live" status text

Keep API endpoints as /api/images/* since they manage container images.
Only the nav link and page route use /sandboxes.

Also remove the "live" text from the header status indicator, keeping
just the green dot glow.

feat(gateway): auto-detect browser timezone via Intl.DateTimeFormat

Send the browser's IANA timezone in the WebSocket connect frame and
auto-persist it to USER.md on first connect. The timezone flows through
the prompt runtime context with explicit user config taking priority
over the browser-detected value.

- Add timezone field to ConnectParams (protocol) and ConnectedClient
- Send Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone in ws-connect.js
- Auto-persist to USER.md when no timezone is configured yet
- Forward _timezone through chat.send, chat.raw_prompt, chat.full_context
- Fall back to browser timezone in build_prompt_runtime_context
- Add accept_language, remote_ip, timezone to PromptHostRuntimeContext
- Extract real client IP from proxy headers in ws_upgrade_handler
- Inject TZ env var into Docker and Apple Container sandboxes

fix(cron): skip heartbeat when no prompt configured, fix duplicate runs

Two fixes:

1. Heartbeat no longer fires when there is nothing to check. When neither
   a config prompt nor HEARTBEAT.md content exists, the job is not
   created/enabled instead of falling back to a generic default prompt
   that wastes LLM calls.

2. Fix race condition causing duplicate cron executions. process_due_jobs()
   collected due jobs under a read lock and spawned them via tokio::spawn,
   but running_at_ms was only set inside the spawned task. Before that
   write happened, the timer loop re-entered process_due_jobs and spawned
   duplicates. Now running_at_ms is set under a write lock before spawning.

feat(metrics): populate cache token counters from provider responses

Add cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens fields to the Usage struct
and wire them through all LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compat,
async_openai, genai, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, Codex) and all three
metrics recording sites (provider_chain, runner, chat). The Prometheus
counters CACHE_READ_TOKENS_TOTAL and CACHE_WRITE_TOKENS_TOTAL were
already defined but never populated — they now reflect actual API usage.

Also add uptime, active session, connected client, and WebSocket
connection gauges to the metrics snapshot loop and remove the unused
LiveIndicator from the charts section.

feat(tools): add get_user_location tool with browser geolocation

Allow the LLM to request the user's geographic coordinates via the
browser Geolocation API. The flow: tool call → WebSocket event →
browser permission popup → coordinates sent back via RPC → cached
in memory and persisted to USER.md → included in system prompt.

Key changes:
- Timezone newtype wrapping chrono_tz::Tz, GeoLocation struct
- LocationTool with LocationRequester trait for gateway decoupling
- location.request/location.result WS event + RPC pair
- GatewayLocationRequester using PendingInvoke oneshot pattern
- Browser handler with 1-hour maximumAge cache
- Location field in PromptHostRuntimeContext (host line)

feat(gateway): add logs download, compression, CORS security, and tower middleware stack

Add a Download button to the logs page that streams the JSONL log file
via GET /api/logs/download with gzip/zstd compression.

Harden the gateway middleware stack:
- Replace allow_origin(Any) with dynamic host-based CORS validation

  protection, secure for Docker/cloud deployments with unknown hostnames
- Add CatchPanicLayer to convert handler panics to 500 responses
- Add RequestBodyLimitLayer (16 MiB) to prevent memory exhaustion
- Add SetSensitiveHeadersLayer to redact Authorization/Cookie in traces
- Add security response headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options,

- Add SetRequestIdLayer + PropagateRequestIdLayer for x-request-id
  correlation across HTTP request logs
- Enable zstd compression alongside gzip for better ratios
- Consolidate layer application into apply_middleware_stack() with
  documented ordering

feat(sandbox): add image, audio, media, and data processing packages

Expand default sandbox packages with tools for headless image
manipulation (imagemagick, vips, pngquant, webp, exiftool), audio/video
processing (ffmpeg, sox, lame, flac, opus), and data conversion
(pandoc, poppler-utils, csvtool, miller, datamash).

feat(sandbox): add document, office, and search packages

Add LaTeX (texlive-latex-base/extra/fonts-recommended), legacy office
converters (antiword, catdoc, unrtf), headless LibreOffice

feat(sandbox): add GIS and OpenStreetMap packages

Add gdal-bin (ogr2ogr for OSM/GeoJSON/Shapefile conversion),
mapnik-utils + python3-mapnik (render OSM to PNG/SVG), osm2pgsql

feat(tools): add sandbox_packages tool for on-demand package discovery

Instead of injecting the full package list into every system prompt,
expose a read-only sandbox_packages tool the LLM calls only when it
needs to know what's installed (image processing, audio/video, document
conversion, GIS, etc.).

The tool reads SandboxRouter config, filters out infrastructure deps
(lib*, *-dev, fonts-*), and returns packages grouped by category.

feat(sandbox): add communication packages, hybrid sandbox query, and mise

Add CalDAV (vdirsyncer, khal), email (isync, notmuch, aerc, mutt,
neomutt), newsgroups (tin, slrn), and Discord (python3-discord)
packages to default sandbox packages. All verified as available in
Ubuntu 24.04 (noble).

Update sandbox_packages tool with hybrid mode: always returns the
categorized config list, and when a sandbox container is already
running, queries dpkg-query to report any additional packages
installed at runtime.

Install mise (jdx/mise) in the sandbox Dockerfile template so users
can easily install up-to-date software inside containers. Bump
Dockerfile template version to v4 to force image rebuild.

refactor(gateway): consolidate GatewayState per-field RwLocks into single RwLock<GatewayInner>

Replace ~22 individual RwLock fields on GatewayState with a single
RwLock<GatewayInner> struct. Since GatewayState is always behind Arc,
the nested Arc<RwLock<T>> pattern was unnecessary overhead.

- Create GatewayInner holding all mutable runtime state as plain types
- Keep immutable fields (auth, services, credential_store, etc.) directly
  on GatewayState for lock-free access
- Keep AtomicU64/AtomicUsize fields lock-free on the outer struct
- Remove approval_manager (never accessed via GatewayState at runtime)
- Remove webauthn_state (only used in AuthState, passed separately)
- Consolidate adjacent lock acquisitions (e.g. hooks.list reads both
  discovered_hooks and hook_registry in one guard)
- Update all 10 consumer files to use state.inner.read/write().await

feat(telegram): add location sharing with live location tracking

Enable Telegram users to share their geographic location, updating the
cached location in GatewayInner and persisting it to USER.md. Supports
both one-shot and live (continuous) location sharing — live updates
arrive as EditedMessage and are processed silently without dispatching
to the LLM.

- Add Location variant to ChannelMessageKind and update_location() to
  ChannelEventSink trait
- Add extract_location() in telegram handlers with live_period detection
- Handle EditedMessage in polling loop for silent live location updates
- Add updated_at timestamp to GeoLocation with human-readable Display
  (e.g. "48.8566,2.3522 (updated 5m ago)")
- Persist location_updated_at in USER.md YAML frontmatter
- Add request_channel_location() to LocationRequester trait for
  tool-triggered location requests via Telegram
- Implement GatewayLocationRequester::request_channel_location() using
  PendingInvoke pattern with 60s timeout

refactor(mcp): consolidate McpManager per-field RwLocks into single RwLock<McpManagerInner>

Same pattern as the GatewayState refactoring: replace 3 independent
RwLocks (clients, tools, registry) with a single RwLock<McpManagerInner>.
This eliminates inconsistency windows between sequential writes and
provides atomic snapshots across all fields.

Key changes:
- Introduce McpManagerInner struct behind single RwLock
- stop_server atomically removes client+tools, drops lock before shutdown
- start_server does network work outside lock, then atomic insert
- status_all/tool_bridges use single read lock for consistent snapshots
- Remove registry_read()/registry_write() that leaked lock guards
- Update mcp_service.rs to use registry_snapshot() instead

fix(gateway): collapse nested if in ws timezone handling (clippy)

fix(agents): make openai-codex token refresh async to prevent runtime panic

get_valid_token() used block_on inside std::thread::scope from an async
context, causing "Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime" panics
when refreshing expired OAuth tokens. Now fully async with .await.

fix(gateway): ensure session row exists before setting channel binding

set_channel_binding() uses UPDATE which silently no-ops when the session
row doesn't exist yet. For brand-new Telegram sessions (first message),
the row hasn't been created at that point, so the binding is never
persisted. This causes get_user_location to fail with "no channel
binding for session".

Fix by calling upsert() (INSERT ON CONFLICT) when the session row is
missing, not just when it exists with a NULL binding.

fix(sessions): use blocking file lock to prevent concurrent write failures

replace_history() so concurrent tool-result persists wait for the

security(gateway): implement three-tier authentication model

Replace the simple localhost_only + password check with a per-request
is_local_connection() function that distinguishes direct local
connections from proxied traffic. This prevents auth bypass when Moltis
runs behind a reverse proxy on the same machine (CVE-2026-25253 class).

Three tiers:
1. Password set → always require auth (any IP)
2. No password + local connection → full access (dev convenience)
3. No password + remote/proxied → onboarding only (setup code required)

Local connection detection uses four conditions (all must pass):
- MOLTIS_BEHIND_PROXY env var not set (hard override for bare proxies)
- No proxy headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP, Forwarded)
- Host header resolves to loopback (or absent)
- TCP source IP is loopback

Fixes auth bypass for reverse proxy deployments where all traffic
appears to originate from 127.0.0.1.

feat(sessions): add entity versioning to prevent stale updates

Add a monotonically incrementing version column to the sessions table.
Every mutation (touch, set_model, set_project_id, etc.) atomically
bumps the version in the DB. The version is included in all RPC
responses (list, resolve, patch, fork) and session event broadcasts.

The frontend Session class uses the version as a staleness guard:
incoming data with a lower version than the current value is rejected,
replacing the fragile messageCount-based heuristic. Version=0 is
treated as "unversioned, always accept" for backward compatibility
with existing sessions.

Also adds broadcast from sessions.patch so other tabs/clients learn
about renames, model changes, and other session mutations via
WebSocket events.

projects with component refactoring.

fix(gateway): reactive session badge with optimistic updates

  bumpCount() methods to Session class for proper reactive updates

- Fix /clear not resetting badge by calling syncCounts(0,0) before

the identity save step.

explicit opts, and call it at all four auth-success points in the
onboarding view (password setup, passkey registration, optional

fix(exec): use host data dir when no container runtime is available

When the sandbox mode is "all" (the default) but no container runtime
exists (e.g. DigitalOcean without Docker), the exec tool was setting
the working directory to /home/sandbox which only exists inside
containers.  This caused every exec call to fail with ENOENT.

Now checks whether the backend is a real container runtime before
choosing /home/sandbox as the working directory.  When the backend is
"none", falls back to the host data directory instead.

Also improves the spawn error message to include the missing directory
path instead of the cryptic "No such file or directory (os error 2)".

after processing completed because the code used the non-streaming
`complete()` method. This change enables real-time token streaming even
when tools are available.

- Extend StreamEvent enum with ToolCallStart, ToolCallArgumentsDelta,
  and ToolCallComplete variants for streaming tool calls
- Add stream_with_tools() method to LlmProvider trait with default
  fallback to stream()
- Implement streaming with tools in AnthropicProvider, handling
  content_block_start/delta/stop events for tool_use blocks

  TextDelta events as text arrives while accumulating tool calls
- Update gateway to use the new streaming agent loop

The UI now receives text tokens in real-time via WebSocket delta events,
providing a much better user experience when using Anthropic models with
tools enabled.

WebSocket reconnect, causing stale queued messages to reappear. Now

fix(gateway): never attach model footer or timestamp to user messages

fix(gateway): prevent multi-move race in queued message tray

Extract moveFirstQueuedToChat() with a data-moving flag on the tray
element so that only the first thinking event per LLM run moves a
message from the queue. Multi-iteration runs (tool calls) fire
multiple thinking events; without the flag each one moved a separate
queued message, causing batched responses.

The flag is cleared by handleChatFinal at the end of each run,
readying the tray for the next queued message.

fix(gateway): defer user message persist until after semaphore

Previously, send() persisted the user message to the session store
before checking the per-session semaphore. When the semaphore was
held, the message was queued and returned early — but it had already
been written to the JSONL file. When the queue later replayed the
message via send(), it was persisted a second time, causing
duplicates in the LLM context and duplicate UI renders.

Move the persist call to after the semaphore is acquired. Queued
messages are now only persisted when they actually run. The history
read no longer needs to pop the last entry since the user message
hasn't been appended yet (run_streaming / run_agent_loop append it
themselves).

feat(gateway): add Copy button to full context panel

fix(gateway): move queued messages only after response is rendered

Previously, moveFirstQueuedToChat() was called during the thinking
event, which caused the next queued user message to appear in the
chat BEFORE the current response finished rendering. With
multi-iteration runs (tool calls), this resulted in wrong ordering:
user-msg → next-user-msg → exec-card instead of user-msg →
exec-card → next-user-msg.

Now queued messages are moved from the tray at the END of
handleChatFinal (after all response content is rendered) and in
handleChatError. This gives correct ordering: each user message
appears right before its corresponding response.

Also removes the data-moving flag machinery which is no longer
needed since thinking events no longer move tray messages.

feat(gateway): add client-side message sequence number for ordering diagnostics

on page reload are handled gracefully (no false warnings).

fix(providers): show model selector after OAuth in onboarding

Fix two bugs preventing model selection for OAuth providers:

1. Provider-model filter never matched providers with dashes (e.g.
   github-copilot, openai-codex). The filter stripped dashes from
   the search term but not from the model's provider field, so
   "github-copilot".includes("githubcopilot") always returned false.

2. When an OAuth token already existed (auto-detected at startup),
   startOAuth just marked the provider validated without showing the
   model selector. Now it calls onOAuthAuthenticated which fetches
   available models and presents the selector.

providers.save_key with an empty API key. Adds the same save_model
call to the API-key path for consistency with the settings page.

Use Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) to convert lat/lon into place names when

tool response, so the LLM can reference locations naturally in voice
replies while retaining raw coordinates for precision.

GeoLocation struct gains an optional place field persisted in USER.md.
Cached locations with an existing place derive the short name by
splitting on the first comma. Gracefully falls back to raw coordinates
if reverse geocoding fails.

shared AudioContext on send (chat and voice) to unlock playback for

feat(agents): retry once on transient LLM provider errors

When a provider returns a 5xx, overloaded, or server_error response,
retry once after a 2-second delay before surfacing the error. Applies
to both streaming and non-streaming agent loops. The failed attempt
does not count toward the iteration limit.

Adds RetryingAfterError runner event so the gateway can broadcast
retry status to the frontend. Also integrates VOICE_REPLY_SUFFIX
into the chat run_with_tools path when reply medium is voice.

The location tool description now explicitly tells the LLM to use

imprecise for search engines. Place names are reserved for voice

fix(onboarding): improve scroll padding in channel and summary steps

feat(tools): add show_map tool and location precision modes

Add `show_map` LLM tool that composes static map images from OSM tiles
with red/blue marker pins (destination + user location), clickable links
to Google Maps, Apple Maps, and OpenStreetMap, and auto-zoom when both
positions are provided. Includes ImageMagick CLI fallback when in-process
tile compositing fails.

Add `precision` parameter to `get_user_location` tool with two modes:
- "precise" (default): GPS-level (~5-20m), enableHighAccuracy, 1min cache
- "coarse": city-level (~1-5km), faster, 30min cache

The LLM chooses the mode based on the query — precise for nearby places
and walking directions, coarse for flights, weather, and time zones.

fix(tools): use place names in map links and skip Brave when unconfigured

Map links now search by place name (e.g. "Tartine Bakery") instead of

Web search skips the Brave API call entirely when no API key is configured
and goes straight to DuckDuckGo, avoiding a wasted round-trip and
preventing the LLM from retrying on the same "not configured" error.

fix(tools): block DuckDuckGo fallback for 1h after CAPTCHA

When DuckDuckGo returns a CAPTCHA challenge, subsequent calls now fail
instantly instead of making another network round-trip that will also
fail. The cooldown lasts 1 hour, after which DDG is retried.

The error message tells the LLM that search is unavailable and suggests
configuring BRAVE_API_KEY or PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, preventing it from
burning iterations on repeated retries.

fix(voice): add autoplay debug logging, stop audio on mic, Esc cancels

Pressing Escape while recording cancels the mic without sending —

security(gateway): implement three-tier authentication model

Replace the simple localhost_only + password check with a per-request
is_local_connection() function that distinguishes direct local
connections from proxied traffic. This prevents auth bypass when Moltis
runs behind a reverse proxy on the same machine (CVE-2026-25253 class).

Three tiers:
1. Password set → always require auth (any IP)
2. No password + local connection → full access (dev convenience)
3. No password + remote/proxied → onboarding only (setup code required)

Local connection detection uses four conditions (all must pass):
- MOLTIS_BEHIND_PROXY env var not set (hard override for bare proxies)
- No proxy headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP, Forwarded)
- Host header resolves to loopback (or absent)
- TCP source IP is loopback

Fixes auth bypass for reverse proxy deployments where all traffic
appears to originate from 127.0.0.1.

feat(sessions): add entity versioning to prevent stale updates

Add a monotonically incrementing version column to the sessions table.
Every mutation (touch, set_model, set_project_id, etc.) atomically
bumps the version in the DB. The version is included in all RPC
responses (list, resolve, patch, fork) and session event broadcasts.

The frontend Session class uses the version as a staleness guard:
incoming data with a lower version than the current value is rejected,
replacing the fragile messageCount-based heuristic. Version=0 is
treated as "unversioned, always accept" for backward compatibility
with existing sessions.

Also adds broadcast from sessions.patch so other tabs/clients learn

fix(config): resolve lock reentrancy deadlock in update_config

discover_and_load() called save_config() when the loaded config had
port == 0, which re-acquires CONFIG_SAVE_LOCK. When called from
update_config() (which already holds the lock), this deadlocked on
the non-reentrant std::sync::Mutex.

This manifested in CI where concurrent nextest processes could race
on the shared ~/.moltis/moltis.toml file, leaving a config with
port = 0 that triggered the reentrant lock path.

Fix:
- Use save_config_to_path() directly in discover_and_load() to
  bypass the lock (safe because the caller already holds it or
  there is no concurrent mutation to guard against)
- Isolate auth_middleware integration tests with per-process temp
  config/data directories via set_config_dir/set_data_dir
- Add slow-timeout with terminate-after to nextest CI profile so
  hung tests are killed after 120s instead of blocking forever

On proxy deployments (Render+Cloudflare), the auth middleware returns

onboarding app was eagerly connecting WS on page load before auth
was set up, causing infinite 401 retry spam.

Move connectWs() out of onboarding-app.js and into an
ensureWsConnected() helper in onboarding-view.js that fires once —
either after auth completes (step 0 → 1) or immediately when auth
is not needed. Also downgrades the QMD "not installed" log from
warn to info per logging guidelines.

Move DEFAULT_SOUL from agents::prompt to config::loader so the config
crate owns all workspace-file I/O. load_soul() now seeds SOUL.md with
the default soul text when the file doesn't exist, mirroring how
discover_and_load() writes moltis.toml on first run. If the file is
deleted it gets re-seeded on next load.

fix(config): prevent SOUL.md re-seeding after explicit clear

save_soul(None) now writes an empty file instead of deleting SOUL.md.
This lets load_soul() distinguish "user cleared the soul" (empty file →

Without this, clearing the soul via settings would immediately re-create
the default on the next load_soul() call in the response.

feat(cron): add event-driven heartbeat wake with system events queue

Add three integration patterns so agents and background exec can trigger
the heartbeat organically:

  the heartbeat drains. Background processes enqueue events; the heartbeat
  prepends summaries to the LLM prompt via build_event_enriched_prompt().

- CronWakeMode on cron jobs: `Now` triggers an immediate heartbeat after
  the job fires; `NextHeartbeat` (default) waits for the next tick.

- Exec completion callback: ExecTool fires ExecCompletionFn after every
  command, which enqueues a summary event and wakes the heartbeat.

always processes noteworthy events. Multiple wake() calls coalesce

fix(voice): improve voice reply prompt and audio player placement

Tell the LLM that the user is speaking via voice and their messages are
speech-to-text transcriptions so it doesn't respond with "I can't hear
you." Also fix the "Voice it" button to render the audio player above the
text (matching the reload/history behavior) instead of below it.

fix(voice): deliver TTS audio even when text was streamed

When streaming is enabled for a Telegram channel, the text gets
delivered via edit-in-place and the target is marked as streamed.
The final delivery step was skipping streamed targets entirely,
which meant the TTS voice audio was never sent back.

Now voice-medium targets bypass the stream dedupe so TTS audio is
always delivered. When text was already streamed, only the voice
audio is sent (no duplicate caption or text follow-up).

Also update the voice reply system prompt to tell the LLM that the
user is speaking via voice (speech-to-text transcription) so it
doesn't respond with "I can't hear you."

Also fix the "Voice it" button audio player to render above the text
(matching the reload/history layout) instead of below it.

fix(tools): don't register web_search tool when API key is missing

When no search API key is configured and DuckDuckGo fallback is
disabled, the web_search tool was still offered to the LLM, which
would call it and always get an error back. Now `from_config`
returns None in this case so the tool is not registered at all.

fix(agents): don't emit regular text as ThinkingText when alongside tool calls

When the LLM produces text and tool calls in the same iteration (e.g. a
search result table followed by a `browser close` cleanup call), the
text was emitted as ThinkingText and displayed as reasoning in the web
UI instead of as a regular message. The final iteration (empty text
after the cleanup tool) then returned a silent/empty response.

Fix both streaming and non-streaming paths:
- Only emit ThinkingText for actual extended-thinking reasoning, not for
  regular text that happens to appear alongside tool calls
- Track answer text across iterations via `last_answer_text` so the
  final response falls back to it when the last iteration is empty

fix(ci): only tag Docker image as latest for highest semver release (#211)

When multiple version tags are pushed simultaneously, concurrent
merge-docker jobs race to set the `latest` and `major.minor` tags.
The last job to finish wins regardless of version ordering — this
caused v0.9.9 to overwrite v0.9.10 as `latest`.

Add a pre-step that queries GitHub tags API to determine the highest
semver tag. Floating tags (`latest`, `{{major}}.{{minor}}`) are only
applied when the current tag matches the highest version. Per-version
and sha tags are always applied.

transparently with the authentication flow: it initializes on first

fix(import): resolve OpenClaw workspace from config and cross-machine paths

The workspace resolver only checked ~/.openclaw/workspace, ignoring the
agents.defaults.workspace field in openclaw.json. When the config points
to a path from another machine (e.g. /root/clawd), the workspace was
never found — causing the onboarding import step to show categories as
"(not found)" despite ~/.openclaw being detected.

Now resolve_workspace_dir reads the config workspace field, tries the
exact path, then remaps the basename under ~/ for cross-machine setups,
and falls back to ~/clawd as a well-known convention. Same remap logic
added to per-agent workspace resolution in agents.rs.

feat(protocol): upgrade WebSocket protocol from v3 to v4 (#247)

* feat(protocol): upgrade WebSocket protocol from v3 to v4

Implement 7 protocol features for a generic, self-describing WebSocket
protocol:

1. Subscribe/Unsubscribe — clients opt-in to event streams instead of
   receiving all events; v3 clients default to wildcard (all events)
2. Extension-based Connect — v4 connect params with namespaced
   extensions separate protocol-core from app-specific fields
3. Standardized Error Codes — 10 new semantic codes (UNAUTHORIZED,
   FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RATE_LIMITED, TIMEOUT, INTERNAL,
   PROTOCOL_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, UNKNOWN_METHOD)
4. Bidirectional RPC — server can send req frames to clients and
   receive res frames back via oneshot channels
5. Stream Primitive — stream/done fields on EventFrame for chunked
   LLM token delivery
6. Channel Multiplexing — optional channel field on all frames for
   scoping events to logical channels
7. Schema Discovery — system.describe method returns protocol schema
   with method and event descriptors

Backward compatible: v3 clients connect with wildcard subscriptions,
flat connect params, and existing error codes still work.

container runtimes and bare host execution. When no Docker daemon or Apple

* fix(db): enable WAL mode on moltis.db and memory.db

Simple INSERTs into sessions and metrics_history were taking 3–10 s
because moltis.db and memory.db used the default journal_mode=DELETE
with synchronous=FULL.  Under concurrent writers this causes exclusive
lock contention — one writer blocks until the other finishes its fsync.

Switch both pools (and the swift-bridge's second pool on the same file)
to journal_mode=WAL + synchronous=NORMAL, matching the fix already
applied to metrics.db.  WAL allows concurrent readers + one writer
without blocking, and NORMAL sync avoids the extra fsync per commit.

* fix(memory): wrap batch DB operations in transactions

The memory sync was issuing hundreds of individual auto-committed
INSERTs (one per chunk, one per embedding cache entry), each taking
the write lock and fsyncing independently.  This caused concurrent
writers (sessions, metrics) to queue behind the entire batch, leading
to 3-10 s delays on trivial single-row INSERTs.

- Add put_cached_embeddings_batch() to MemoryStore trait and impls

fix(web): read DOM value in identity blur handlers to prevent stale closure skip

The onNameBlur/onUserNameBlur handlers captured useState values from
the previous Preact render cycle. When Playwright (or fast user input)
fires blur immediately after fill, the batched state update from the
input event hasn't committed yet, so the blur handler sees the old
value. Since old value == server value, autoSaveNameField returned
early and the save never fired.

Fix by reading e.target.value (always current) instead of the stale
closure variable. Also cancel lingering flashSaved timers so
back-to-back saves don't have the first timer prematurely clear the
second "Saved" indicator.

fix(security): reject cross-origin WebSocket upgrades (CSWSH protection)

Mitigates the same class of vulnerability as GHSA-g8p2-7wf7-98mq in
openclaw: a malicious webpage could connect to the local gateway WebSocket
from the victim's browser, gaining full operator access because loopback
connections are auto-authenticated.

The fix validates the Origin header on WebSocket upgrade requests.
Browsers always send Origin on cross-origin requests; non-browser clients
(CLI, SDKs) typically omit it and are still allowed through. Loopback
variants (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) are treated as equivalent.

feat(agents): add model failover with per-provider circuit breakers

When an LLM provider call fails with a retryable error (rate limit, auth,
server error, billing exhaustion), automatically try the next available
provider instead of returning an error to the user. Failover order
prioritizes same model on a different backend, then other models from the
same provider, then other providers entirely.

Each provider tracks consecutive failures via a circuit breaker (3 failures
→ 60s cooldown) to avoid hammering broken endpoints. Context window and
invalid request errors are never retried since they would fail everywhere.

Configurable via `[failover]` in moltis.toml (enabled by default).

fix(cron): add delay_ms to avoid LLM computing absolute timestamps (#377)

The 'at' schedule kind previously required the LLM to supply at_ms as
an absolute epoch millisecond value. LLMs reliably miscalculate this
(training-data clock skew means 'now' is off by months or years),
causing one-shot jobs to be scheduled in the past and never fire.

Add delay_ms (aliases: delayMs, delay, in, in_ms, offset_ms) as a
server-resolved relative offset: the tool computes now_ms + delay_ms
at call time, so the LLM only needs to express durations (e.g. 600000
for 10 minutes) rather than absolute timestamps.

Existing at_ms is preserved for callers that have a real absolute time.

fix(gateway): retain proxy shutdown sender to prevent immediate proxy exit (#368)

The `watch::Sender` for the trusted-network proxy was declared inside the
`#[cfg(feature = "trusted-network")]` block and dropped at block exit,
causing the proxy task to receive an immediate shutdown signal. Move the
sender into `PreparedGateway` so it lives as long as the server.

Fixes #367

fix(tools): only expose exec node parameter when nodes are connected

The exec tool unconditionally added a `node` parameter to its schema
whenever a NodeExecProvider was attached, which happened at startup
regardless of config. This caused the LLM to hallucinate node values
like "host", producing "node 'host' not found or not connected" errors
even when no nodes were configured or connected.

Gate the `node` schema parameter and the "or a remote node" description
on a live connected-node count. A shared `Arc<AtomicUsize>` is
incremented on node register and decremented on unregister, allowing
the sync `parameters_schema()` path to check without awaiting the
inner RwLock.

fix(agents): sanitize model-mangled tool names from parallel calls

Some LLM providers (notably Kimi K2.5 via OpenRouter) mangle tool names
when generating parallel tool calls by appending numeric suffixes
(exec → exec_2, browser → browser_4) or adding a functions_ prefix
(spawn_agent → functions_spawn_agent_6).

- Return Cow<str> to avoid unnecessary allocations

is visible in logs. No legitimate tool name (built-in or MCP) ends with
`_\d+`, so there are no false positives.

fix(provider-setup): include lmstudio in known_providers and replace ollama name checks

PR #286 added LM Studio as a first-class OpenAI-compatible provider in
crates/providers but missed integrating it with crates/provider-setup.
The result is that the UI shows lmstudio in pickers like Pin Models and
Available Providers, but providers.save_models / save_key reject it
with "unknown provider: lmstudio" because known_providers() never
returned an entry for it.

This change:

  * Adds lmstudio to known_providers() with key_optional=true to match
    its actual behaviour (LM Studio's local server doesn't require auth).

  * Replaces the four `name == "ollama"` / `name != "ollama"` string
    checks with a typed KnownProvider::is_local_only() helper that
    returns true for any provider whose key is optional or whose
    auth_type is Local. This honours the CLAUDE.md "match on types,
    never strings" guideline and is exactly the cleanup PR #286's own
    description called out as a goal.

  * Adds regression tests covering known_providers content, env_key
    mapping, save_key acceptance, available() listings (cloud and
    local mode), and a structural check that the new is_local_only
    helper covers the same set as the old name-based check.

Closes #599

fix(provider-setup): add dedicated local_only field to KnownProvider

Decouple the `is_local_only()` check from `key_optional` by adding an
explicit `local_only: bool` field. A remote provider could legitimately
support unauthenticated access without binding to localhost, so using
`key_optional` as a proxy for local-only was misleading.

Also rename `is_local_only_matches_legacy_name_check` to
`is_local_only_is_superset_of_legacy_check` and clarify the comment to
reflect the intentional one-directional (superset) assertion.

fix(mcp): normalize loopback redirect URIs to http for OAuth registration

RFC 8252 §8.3 mandates the `http` scheme for loopback redirect URIs.
Strict authorization servers (e.g. Attio) reject `https://localhost`
during dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) with `invalid_redirect_uri`,
breaking MCP OAuth on single-host deployments where the web UI is served
over TLS on `https://localhost:<port>`.

Rewrite the scheme from `https` to `http` when the redirect URI host is
a loopback identifier (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`). The main TLS
listener's peek-based HTTP→HTTPS redirect in `moltis_tls` transparently
bounces the plain-HTTP OAuth callback back onto the real HTTPS callback
handler, preserving path and query string, so the flow completes without
any additional listener, gateway, or UI changes.

Non-loopback hosts (`moltis.lan`, real TLS hostnames) are untouched and
continue to use the web-origin HTTPS callback, which is a legitimate
confidential-client redirect URI unaffected by §8.3.

Tests: 10 unit tests covering the normalizer matrix (localhost, IPv4/IPv6
loopback, case-insensitivity, real hostnames, non-loopback IPv4, http
scheme passthrough, path/query preservation, unparseable input) plus an
integration test that drives `start_web_oauth_flow` with a mockito AS and
asserts the registration body and authorization URL use the rewritten
HTTP form.

Fixes #629

feat(chat): implement recency_preserving compaction mode

Second child of the compaction-modes epic (moltis-dxw). Implements the
head + middle-marker + tail strategy from hermes-agent's context
compressor and openclaw's tool-pair repair, with zero LLM calls.

Strategy:
- Protect the first `protect_head` messages verbatim (system prompt +
  first exchange).
- Walk backward from the end accumulating tokens until the tail budget
  (`threshold_percent × tail_budget_ratio × context_window`) is
  consumed, with `protect_tail_min` as a floor so short sessions still
  keep the configured minimum. Never split a tool_call/tool_result
  group — the boundary slides forward past any consecutive tool-result
  run.
- Collapse the middle region into a single marker user message that
  counts each role and notes "Recent messages preserved verbatim
  below", so the LLM retry has a quick sense of what was elided.
- After splicing, replace any bulky tool-result content in the retained
  slice with a placeholder string (cheap pre-pass — catches multi-KB
  tool outputs that would blow the context window on their own).
- Repair orphaned tool_use / tool_result pairs so strict providers
  (Anthropic, OpenAI strict mode) accept the retry:
  - Tool results whose parent assistant tool_call was dropped → removed.
  - Assistant tool_calls whose results were dropped → stub tool result
    inserted immediately after the parent, keyed on the tool_call_id.
- If the head and tail already overlap (tiny session) AND there's no
  bulky tool-result content to prune in place, return a clear
  `TooSmallToCompact` error that points the user at `deterministic` so
  callers don't end up in a no-op compact loop.

fix(chat): memory-file summary lookup across all compaction modes

The ChatService::compact path wrote the post-compaction memory-file
snapshot and the AfterCompaction hook's `summary_len` field from
`compacted[0].content` with a best-effort "[Conversation Summary]"
prefix strip. That worked for deterministic and llm_replace (both of
which leave a single summary message at index 0) but was wrong for
recency_preserving and structured, where the first message in the
compacted history is the verbatim head message (e.g. "user 0"), not
the summary.

Introduce `compaction_run::extract_summary_body`, a best-effort helper
that walks the compacted history for the first message whose content
begins with either "[Conversation Summary]" (produced by deterministic,
structured, and llm_replace) or "[Conversation Compacted]" (produced
by the recency_preserving middle marker), and returns the stripped
body. Returns "" when no summary-shaped message is found, which is
benign — the memory file still gets written, just without a body, and
the hook payload's summary_len is 0.

Unit tests cover the three relevant cases: summary prefix at index 0,
compacted marker mid-list, and no summary-shaped message present.

Also add a regression test that exercises iterative re-compaction end
to end: a StubProvider captures whether any forwarded ChatMessage
contains a unique needle, runs `structured_strategy` against a history
whose first message is a previous compaction summary containing the
needle, and asserts the provider actually saw it in the prompt. This
pins the structured mode's iterative-compaction behaviour against
regressions in the prompt-assembly code.

Stub provider grew `with_needle` / `saw_needle` interior-mutability
helpers using Arc<Mutex<bool>> (not Mutex<()>, per CLAUDE.md — the
mutex guards real state). No other behaviour changes.

fix(web): track compacting status message per-session to avoid removing compact card

Addresses Greptile P1 on PR #653 (thread PRRT_kwDOREW6tc56UEUC).

When `send()` triggers pre-emptive auto-compaction, the broadcast
sequence is:

  1. auto_compact start    — appends "Compacting conversation…"
  2. chat.compact done     — (new in this PR) emitted by self.compact()
  3. auto_compact done     — emitted by send() after self.compact()

`S.chatMsgBox.lastChild` and then render the compact card. That
worked when there was only an `auto_compact done` event — `lastChild`
was always the status message. With the new `chat.compact done`
handler (`handleChatCompact`) now rendering the card at step 2,
`lastChild` at step 3 is the compact card itself, so the old
pattern removed the card instead of the status message. The

`removeCompactingStatus(p)` helper before rendering the card. The
helper:

- Looks up the stored element for the session key.
- Deletes the map entry unconditionally.
- Removes the element from `chatMsgBox` only if it's still a child
  (defensive — guards against stale references after session
  switches).

The `shouldRenderCompactCard` debounce still ensures the card
renders exactly once across the three possible event sequences:

  send() auto-compact:      start → compact done (card) → auto_compact done (no-op)
  run_with_tools overflow:  start → auto_compact done (removes status + card)
  manual /compact RPC:      compact done (no status, just card)

`removeCompactingStatus` helper so error messages after a
broken compaction don't accidentally remove whatever happened

from `CompactionOutcome::broadcast_metadata()`, so it carries the
mode/token fields inline. The `send()` pre-emptive path goes
through `self.compact()` which broadcasts a separate `chat.compact
done` event with the metadata, leaving the wrapping `auto_compact
done` metadata-free. A webhook/hook consumer watching `auto_compact
done` would see different shapes depending on which code path
fired.

`auto_compact done` broadcasts so consumers can tell the two paths
apart:

- `"wrapper"` — self-contained (run_with_tools path); mode/token
  metadata is inline on this event.
- `"inner"`   — companion event (send() path); mode/token metadata
  lives on the separate `chat.compact done` event fired from within
  `self.compact()`.

The discriminator is documented inline in both sites so future
consumers know to branch on it when they need metadata. A full
refactor that unified the two paths would require threading
`CompactionOutcome` through `self.compact()`'s return type, which
breaks the existing JSON-RPC response shape. The discriminator
avoids that refactor while giving consumers a clear signal.

fix(agents): detect and break tool-call reflex loops (#658)

Runner previously dispatched tool calls with empty or malformed args
straight to tool.execute without pre-validation, then had no detection
for repeated identical failures. A model stuck in a reflex-retry loop
(e.g. exec({}) on every iteration) would burn through all 25 iterations
before max_iterations fired, producing a ~4 minute dead zone with no
visible progress.

1. Pre-dispatch schema validation (tool_arg_validator.rs): each tool
   call's arguments are checked against the tool's parameters_schema
   before execute() runs. Missing required fields or top-level type
   mismatches short-circuit to a structured, directive error that
   names the failure, echoes the args, and tells the model not to
   retry with identical arguments.

2. Loop detector with escalating intervention (tool_loop_detector.rs):
   tracks a ring buffer of recent (tool, args_hash, error_hash)
   outcomes. Three consecutive failures sharing the same tool and
   (args OR error) fire stage 1 (inject a strong directive
   intervention message). A fourth consecutive failure after the
   nudge fires stage 2 (strip tool schemas for one turn, forcing a
   text response). Any successful tool call resets the state.

   emitted only after validation passes; rejected calls emit a new
   ToolCallRejected event so the UI stops showing "Executing..." for
   calls that never executed. The streaming tool-call accumulator
   logs each finalized args string at debug level to aid diagnosis

fix(agents): loop detector handles mixed-outcome batches correctly (#658)

Two P2 edge cases surfaced by the second Greptile review (PR #664):

1. **False intervention after trailing success in the same batch.** When a
   batch was `[fail, fail, success]` and the detector was one failure away
   from the window, the fail that pushed the window full would set a
   pending nudge, the trailing success would reset the detector, and the
   runner would still inject the stale intervention after the batch.

2. **Stage-skip when both escalations fire within one batch.** A parallel
   batch like `[fail, fail, fail, fail]` would fire `InjectNudge` on the
   third call and `StripTools` on the fourth. The old per-call accumulator
   shadowed the nudge with the strip action, robbing the model of its
   chance to recover via plain text before tools were stripped.

The fix changes both result-processing loops to derive the intervention
action from the detector's *post-batch state* rather than from per-call
`record()` return values:

- Add `consume_pending_action()` on the detector. It looks at the current
  `stage` plus a new internal `nudge_delivered` flag and returns the
  correct single action, one-shotting stage transitions so the same
  intervention can't be applied twice. When it would advance to
  `StripTools` without having delivered a nudge first, it demotes back to
  `Nudged` and returns `InjectNudge` so the nudge lands first; strip-tools
  can fire on the next batch if the pattern persists.

- Extract the intervention-application logic into a single helper,
  `apply_loop_detector_intervention`, shared by the streaming and
  non-streaming runner loops. This eliminates duplicated match arms and
  ensures both paths stay in sync.

Regression coverage:

- `tool_loop_detector::tests` — 5 new unit tests covering
  `consume_pending_action` behaviour for all stage/delivered combinations,
  trailing-success suppression, and the stage-skip guard.
- `runner::tests::mixed_batch_with_trailing_success_does_not_fire_intervention`
  — end-to-end, a parallel batch `[exec({}), exec({}), exec("true")]`
  must not emit any `LoopInterventionFired` event because the trailing
  success recovers cleanly.
- `runner::tests::parallel_batch_with_stage_skip_delivers_nudge_first` —
  end-to-end, a parallel batch of four identical `exec({})` calls must
  emit a stage-1 `LoopInterventionFired` first, not jump straight to
  stage 2.

fix(providers): collapse type arrays in strict mode patching (#716)

Gemini via OpenRouter rejects tool schemas with type arrays like
type: [object, string] because Gemini cannot represent union
types. OpenAI strict mode also requires type to be a single string.

The cron tool (and others) use type arrays for fields like schedule
and payload. When OpenRouter translates these to Gemini's
function_declarations, the union type is lossy — properties may be
dropped while required entries persist, causing INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Fix by extending patch_schema_for_strict_mode to detect type arrays
containing object (via new type_is_object helper) and collapse
them to object. This triggers the existing strict mode path:
additionalProperties: false, required rebuild from properties keys,
and optional fields made nullable.

The collapse is correct for tool calling because:
- The object form is the intended structured shape
- Bare strings/integers are convenience shorthand for non-tool contexts
- OpenAI strict mode already prohibits type arrays

Tests: 6 unit tests + 6 integration tests covering collapse behavior,
nested schemas, non-object arrays (preserved), and end-to-end pipeline.

`finish_reason: "stop"`. Rather than maintaining a hardcoded list of
known tokens or pattern-matching `<|...|>` everywhere (which could
strip legitimate mid-text references to tokenizer tokens), this uses
the structural signal: leaked stop tokens are always the last content
before the stream terminates.

`strip_trailing_stop_tokens` only removes `<|word|>` patterns from
the trailing position of the final response text, preserving any
mid-text occurrences.

exists, so all existing tests passed via the filesystem codepath.

helper that matches on the file-name component. Add tests that explicitly
verify the embedded path returns skills.

fix(tests): stabilize flaky memory_config_get test

Root cause: the memory config test wrote config via `update_config()`
then dispatched the `memory.config.get` handler which re-read from
disk. Concurrent tests (e.g. voice enable) called `discover_and_load()`
which has side-effects (writing defaults.toml, compacting, persisting
random port) that overwrote the temp config file between write and read.

Fix:
- Write TOML config directly to the temp dir (no `update_config()` call
  that can race) with a non-zero port to prevent the port-persistence
  write-back path in `discover_and_load()`.
- Use `discover_and_load_readonly()` in the `memory.config.get` handler
  and in the update test's verification step to avoid write side-effects.
- Guard `test_live_tts_service_enable` with `VoiceConfigTestGuard` since
  its `enable()` path calls `update_config()`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(config): extract initialize_config() from discover_and_load()

discover_and_load() had write side-effects (writing defaults.toml,
compacting config, persisting random port) that ran on every call.
With ~76 call sites across the codebase, concurrent tests sharing a
global config_dir override would race: one test's discover_and_load()
would overwrite another test's temp config file.

Move all write side-effects into a new initialize_config() function
called once at process startup (CLI main, swift-bridge init). Make
discover_and_load() delegate to discover_and_load_readonly() so it
is purely read-only. This eliminates the entire class of config test
races without needing per-test locks or workarounds.

Also guard test_live_tts_service_enable with VoiceConfigTestGuard
since its enable() path calls update_config().

Supersedes the workaround in 8d66dd31.

fix(e2e): stabilize session rename test against onBlur race

The session rename test used fill() followed by press("Enter") on the
input locator. Between these two awaits, the onBlur handler could fire
(triggered by Playwright's internal focus management), calling
commitRename() which sets renaming=false and removes the input from
the DOM before press("Enter") can execute.

Switch to page.keyboard API (focus + Ctrl+A + type + Enter) which
operates on whatever element has focus, avoiding the locator
re-resolution that fails when the input is removed mid-sequence.

fix(config): use atomic writes to prevent moltis.toml corruption

Replace all std::fs::write() calls in config_io.rs with an
atomic_write() helper that writes to a temp file then renames.
This prevents corruption when two processes (CLI + server) write
the config concurrently — rename is atomic on POSIX so readers
always see complete content.

Also add CONFIG_SAVE_LOCK to compact_config() and
save_config_to_path() which previously bypassed the mutex.

Root cause: std::fs::write does open(O_TRUNC) + write(). When
two processes race, one truncates the file but the other's
longer write leaves stale bytes past the shorter write's boundary,
producing invalid TOML (e.g. bare "false" or truncated API keys).

fix(config): use unique temp file for atomic writes

Replace fixed .toml.tmp path with tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in()
so concurrent writers each get a unique temp file in the same
directory. persist() does an atomic rename.

fix(web): command palette keyboard navigation in headless Chromium

ArrowDown/ArrowUp in the command palette failed in headless Chromium
because the onKeyDown handler was on the dialog div, relying on event
bubbling from the focused input. Headless Chromium's form autocomplete
intercepted arrow key events on the input before they could bubble.

- Move onKeyDown from the dialog div to the input element directly
- Add autocomplete="off" to prevent browser autocomplete interference
- Switch useEffect to useLayoutEffect for focus on open, removing the
  requestAnimationFrame wrapper that caused a race condition

fix(web): use capture-phase listener for command palette keyboard nav

ArrowDown/ArrowUp on <input> elements are consumed by headless
Chromium's native autocomplete handling before element-level onKeyDown
handlers fire, even with autocomplete="off". The previous fix (bde900b)
moved the handler from the dialog div to the input, but the browser
still intercepts at the same level.

fix(web): eliminate rAF race in session rename input

The session rename input used requestAnimationFrame to set its value
and focus after mounting. This created a race with Playwright's fill()
method: if fill() started before the rAF callback, the input could
receive a blur event (triggering commitRename and element removal)
before the value was set.

Replace rAF with useLayoutEffect which runs synchronously after render,
before the browser paints, eliminating the timing window. Also guard
commitRename against calls when the input ref is already gone.

Add CLAUDE.md policy: flaky tests must be fixed at the root cause,
never skipped or ignored.

fix(web): prevent session switch from stealing focus during rename

After a session switch completes, switchSession() unconditionally
focused the chat input. If the user was mid-rename (or had any other
input focused), this stole focus, triggered onBlur on the rename input,
and committed/removed it prematurely — causing the E2E test to find the
element detached from the DOM.

Add focusChatInputIfIdle() that skips the focus call when the user is
actively editing another element (document.activeElement is not body
or chatInput).

fix(build): align production feature flags

Define a shared full feature set for the moltis binary and route Docker, package, and release builds through one build wrapper. This keeps Discord and the other production integrations enabled consistently across distributed artifacts while leaving accelerator-specific CUDA/Vulkan builds explicit.

fix(sandbox): wait for image build before launching containers

On a fresh install the sandbox image build runs in a background task
while the server is already accepting requests. If a user sends a
command before the build finishes, `resolve_image()` returns the bare
base image (`ubuntu:25.10`) because `set_global_image()` hasn't been
called yet. The resulting container has none of the pre-installed
packages (tmux, gh, nodejs, etc.), and the fallback `provision_packages`
path cannot install third-party-repo packages (NodeSource, GitHub CLI).

Add a `tokio::sync::Notify` (`build_complete`) to `SandboxRouter`.
The background build task notifies it on completion (success, no-op,
or error). `default_image()` now awaits the notification when
`building_flag` is true, with a 10-minute timeout as a safety net.
This ensures the first exec call gets the fully-provisioned pre-built
image instead of the bare base.

channels_offered, update). With tokio's fair RwLock, if a concurrent

read blocks indefinitely — causing page.goto to hang with zero HTTP
response on CI.

start of build_gon_data, eliminating the deadlock window.

fix(web): move blocking syscalls out of async runtime in build_gon_data

collect_mem_snapshot() calls sysinfo::System::new/refresh_memory/
refresh_processes which are blocking syscalls reading from /proc.
detect_git_branch() does blocking filesystem I/O via gix::discover.

On CI runners with few CPUs, these blocking calls on the async
runtime starve tokio workers, causing concurrent page requests to
time out while health endpoint (which doesn't call build_gon_data)
responds fine.

Wrapped both calls in tokio::task::spawn_blocking so they run on
the blocking thread pool instead of the async worker threads.

Reverted the worker_threads=4 workaround — the proper fix is to not
block the async runtime.

fix(web): wrap remaining blocking I/O in build_gon_data with spawn_blocking

ManifestStore::load() reads the skills manifest from disk via
std::fs::read_to_string on every page request. resolve_channels_offered()
calls find_config_file() + load_config() which do multiple filesystem
stat/read operations. Both ran directly on the async worker thread.

Wrapped both in tokio::task::spawn_blocking to prevent blocking the
async runtime on low-CPU CI runners.

fix(web): bypass std::sync::Mutex in onboarding_completed for async safety

onboarding_completed() called wizard_status() which acquires a
std::sync::Mutex and does filesystem I/O (path.exists()) — both
block the tokio async runtime. On CI runners with few CPUs, this
starves the worker threads, causing page requests to hang.

Replaced with a direct spawn_blocking check of the .onboarded
sentinel file, bypassing the mutex entirely. Verified with local
stress test: 150 concurrent requests with 1 tokio worker = 0 failures.

fix(e2e): restore exec in start-gateway.sh — tee pipe broke process management

The tee pipe (without exec) made the shell script the parent process,
not the gateway. When Playwright kills the shell, the gateway becomes
an orphan still holding the port. The next test retry starts a new
gateway that can't fully initialize because the orphan is still
running. This caused chat-abort and chat-api-message RPC timeouts.

Restored exec so Playwright manages the gateway process directly.
Removed RUST_LOG override and gateway.log artifact (no longer needed
now that the root cause is fixed).

fix(e2e): add 30s timeout to sendRpc shim to prevent hanging on WS drop

On slow CI runners, the WS connection can drop between
waitForWsConnected and the actual sendRpc call. The bundled sendRpc
Promise hangs forever waiting for a response that never arrives,
causing page.evaluate to hang until the 90s test timeout.

Added a 30s Promise.race timeout in the E2E helpers.js shim. The
error message includes "WebSocket disconnected" so every test's
isRetryableRpcError catches it and retries the RPC.
fix(e2e): reduce sendRpc timeout to 1s — RPCs should be instant
fix(e2e): add retry logging to sendRpcFromPage in chat-abort and chat-api-message

fix(ws): eliminate write lock on every WS frame — use AtomicU64 for activity timestamp

The WS handler acquired state.inner.write() on EVERY incoming frame
just to update the client's last_activity timestamp. With tokio's
fair RwLock, this write-lock contention blocked concurrent read locks
(broadcast, RPC dispatch), causing RPC responses to stall.

Changed ClientInfo.last_activity from Instant to AtomicU64 (ms since
process start). The touch() method is now &self with atomic store —
no lock needed. The WS handler uses inner.read() instead of write().

fix(ws): add 30s RPC timeout in sendRpc to detect half-open WS connections

On CI runners, the TCP connection can go half-open (dead but
readyState still OPEN). sendRpc sends the frame into the void and
the Promise hangs forever — the WS onclose never fires so pending
RPCs are never cleaned up.

Added a 30s timeout directly in the TypeScript sendRpc function.
On timeout, the pending entry is cleaned up and the Promise resolves
with a TIMEOUT error containing "WebSocket disconnected" so retry
loops can reconnect. Removed the E2E shim timeout (was 1s, too
aggressive — broke all RPC tests on CI).

fix(ws): add >50ms timing warnings to RPC dispatch and lock acquisition

Every WS RPC now logs a warning if:
- touch read-lock takes >50ms (lock contention)
- RPC dispatch takes >50ms (slow handler)
- broadcast read-lock takes >50ms (lock contention)

Also: 30s RPC timeout in sendRpc (TypeScript) to detect half-open WS,
gateway.log captured to CI artifacts for post-failure analysis.

refactor(gateway): extract ClientRegistry from GatewayInner for lock isolation

Split the hot-path client operations (broadcast, subscribe, touch,
session switch) into a dedicated `ClientRegistryInner` behind its own
`RwLock` on `GatewayState`.

Before: broadcast(read) contended with subscribe(write) on the same
giant RwLock<GatewayInner>. With tokio's fair scheduling, a queued
write blocks all subsequent reads.

After: broadcast uses `client_registry.read()`, subscribe uses
`client_registry.write()` — completely independent from node, config,
session, and auth operations on the old `inner` lock.

Migrated 20+ pure-client lock sites across 7 files:
- broadcast.rs: iterates client_registry instead of inner
- subscribe.rs: modifies subscriptions via client_registry
- channel_mux.rs: join/leave channels via client_registry
- ws.rs: touch uses client_registry.read()
- services.rs: active session lookup
- services/core.rs: session switch, client metadata forwarding
- chat.rs: active session/project lookup

Compound operations (5 sites accessing clients+nodes) still use the
old inner lock — will be addressed in Phase 2.

fix(gateway): complete ClientRegistry migration — remove duplicate fields from GatewayInner

The Phase 1 ClientRegistry extraction left `clients`, `active_sessions`,
and `active_projects` fields in both GatewayInner and ClientRegistryInner.
New client registrations went to client_registry while reads (RPCs,
disconnect, status) still hit the always-empty inner.clients copy.

This caused:
- disconnect_all_clients test failure (draining empty inner.clients)
- CI E2E failures (RPCs looking up clients in wrong HashMap)
- gateway.status reporting 0 connections
- node.invoke failing to find client sender

Remove the duplicate fields from GatewayInner and update all references
to use client_registry. Lock discipline: never hold both inner and
client_registry write locks simultaneously.

fix(e2e): add warmup RPC to waitForWsConnected to verify end-to-end WS

On CI, the WS connection state shows connected/subscribed/OPEN but RPCs
never get responses for the first few tests. Adding a lightweight
'status' RPC round-trip inside waitForWsConnected ensures the WS is
truly functional before tests proceed, not just protocol-level connected.

The poll loop retries with a 2s timeout per attempt, so if the first
connection is broken, it will keep trying until a working connection
is established.

debug(e2e): capture gateway stderr to log file for CI artifact upload

Server-side tracing output (WS connection, RPC dispatch, timing) goes to
