output. Tee stderr to target/e2e-runtime/gateway.log while still
forwarding to Playwright's webServer capture, and include the log in
the E2E test results artifact.

This will reveal whether the server receives RPC frames and what
happens during dispatch — critical for diagnosing the CI-only RPC
timeout issue.

fix(ws): spawn RPC dispatch to prevent read-loop head-of-line blocking

The WS read loop processed RPCs inline with `methods.dispatch(ctx).await`.
If any RPC blocked on a lock (e.g., sessions.switch waiting for inner
write lock during startup), ALL subsequent RPCs on that connection were
queued behind it — causing the 5s timeout on CI where lock contention
is worse due to slower machines.

Spawn each RPC dispatch into its own tokio task. The read loop now
immediately moves to the next frame, and responses are sent back via
the existing client_tx mpsc channel. This eliminates head-of-line
blocking: slow RPCs no longer starve fast ones.

fix(gateway): make chat() lock-free — move chat_override to std::sync::RwLock

The `chat()` method previously acquired `inner.read().await` on every
RPC that touches the chat service. When spawned RPC tasks compete with
background operations holding `inner.write()`, this creates contention
that can block RPCs for seconds — causing CI E2E timeouts.

Move `chat_override` out of `GatewayInner` into a dedicated
`std::sync::RwLock` on `GatewayState`. The `chat()` method is now
synchronous (no await), eliminating the last hot-path dependency on the
`inner` tokio lock for chat RPCs.

This combined with the previous spawned-dispatch fix means chat RPCs
(send, clear, abort, history, etc.) can never be blocked by unrelated
operations holding the inner write lock.

fix(ws): increase sendRpc timeout from 5s to 30s for heavy RPCs

The 5s timeout was too aggressive for RPCs like chat.send that do
real work (provider resolution, tool registration, session persistence,
agent loop spawn). On slow CI runners, these routinely exceed 5s due
to provider registry contention with background model discovery.

30s is a safety net for genuinely broken connections (half-open TCP),
not a performance expectation. Normal RPCs complete in <100ms.

* feat(config): type-safe MCP server policy for agent presets

Replace the `PresetMcpPolicy` struct (with a single `deny_servers:
Vec<String>` field) with a proper enum and a `McpServerId` newtype:

- `All`   — no restrictions, all MCP servers visible (default).
- `Allow` — only listed servers visible; all others denied.
- `Deny`  — all servers visible except listed ones.

The enum encodes mutual exclusivity at the type level instead of
relying on runtime validation. Custom serde keeps TOML backwards
compatible (`deny_servers = [...]` / `allow_servers = [...]`).

`McpServerId` centralises the `mcp__<server>__*` deny-pattern format
in a single `to_deny_pattern()` method.

Policy resolution (Layer 3) now matches on the enum: `Allow` inverts
the list by iterating `config.mcp.servers` keys to deny every server
NOT in the allow-list, so agents can be scoped to a specific subset
of MCP servers — e.g. a restricted kids agent with
`allow_servers = []` gets zero MCP tools.

* refactor(config): reuse McpServerId across MCP boundaries

Use McpServerId instead of plain String in cross-crate MCP type
boundaries:

- ToolSource::Mcp { server: McpServerId } in moltis-agents
- register_mcp() takes McpServerId instead of String
- McpToolBridge stores and returns McpServerId
- McpConfig.servers uses McpServerId as HashMap key
- Borrow<str> impl on McpServerId for ergonomic HashMap lookups

Internal MCP crate types (McpRegistry, McpManager, McpClient) keep
String for now — conversion happens at the bridge boundary. This
follows the CLAUDE.md guidance to define types once in the lower
crate and use them across boundaries.

Add two new fields to AgentPreset, making agents a self-contained
capability boundary:

**PresetSandboxPolicy** — per-agent sandbox overrides:
- mode, network, trusted_domains, workspace_mount, memory_limit,
  cpu_quota — each overrides the global [tools.exec.sandbox] value.
- `apply_to(&mut SandboxConfig)` method for runtime overlay.
- Example: a kids agent with `network = "blocked"` gets no network
  access regardless of the global setting.

**PresetSkillPolicy** — per-agent skill access control:
- allow/deny lists that filter by skill name or category.
- `filter_skills_for_agent()` wired into all three chat service
  entry points (send, run_with_tools, run_streaming).
- Example: a restricted agent with `deny = ["gaming"]` never sees

When an agent preset has sandbox.mode set, apply it as a per-session

with `sandbox.mode = "off"` bypasses sandboxing, regardless of the

The override is set on the router via the existing set_override()

* fix(web): replace broken TOML section-strip regex with line parser

The regex-based approach to strip [mcp]/[sandbox]/[skills] sections
before regenerating them was broken: with the `m` flag, `$` matches
at every line end, so the lazy quantifier stopped after the section
header, leaving key-value lines orphaned. After two save-open-save
cycles, duplicate top-level keys accumulated and caused TOML parse
errors — making the preset permanently unreadable.

Replace with `stripTomlSections()` that walks lines, tracking which
TOML section header is active and skipping lines in named sections.
This correctly removes the entire section including all its keys.

* fix: address greptile 3/5 feedback — sandbox mode dispatch and UI honesty

Two issues identified by Greptile:

1. non-main sandbox mode was mapped to enabled=true, sandboxing all
   sessions including main. Fixed: non-main now removes the override
   and lets the router's global NonMain logic decide correctly.

2. sandbox.network/workspace_mount/memory_limit/cpu_quota are defined
   in the schema but apply_to is never called — they have no runtime
   effect. Removed these fields from the UI to avoid false promises.
   The schema keeps them for when SandboxRouter gains per-session
   config overlays. Only sandbox.mode (which IS enforced) remains
   in the UI.

* fix: clear stale sandbox override when agent has no preset

When the incoming agent_id has no configured preset, the outer
if-let fell through without clearing any previously written sandbox
override. A session migrating from a "no-sandbox" agent to one with
no preset would continue to have sandboxing suppressed.

Add else branch to always remove_override when no preset exists.

* fix(web): correct save error check and preserve sandbox fields

Two issues from Greptile review:

1. Error check used presetToml.trim() instead of tomlToSave to
   determine if the last pending result was a TOML save — save
   failures from structured-only path were never surfaced. Fixed
   by tracking savingToml flag from the computed tomlToSave.

2. sandbox.network and workspace_mount were returned by the API
   but lost on save because they weren't captured in state. Now
   loaded from API response and passed through to TOML generation,
   preserving any manually configured values even though the UI
   only exposes the mode dropdown.

* fix(web): always save preset when capabilities panel is open

When all structured fields were at defaults and the raw TOML only
contained [mcp]/[sandbox]/[skills] sections, tomlToSave was empty
and agents.preset.save was never called — old restrictions survived
silently. Now always save when the capabilities panel was open,
which correctly clears the preset via an empty TOML string.

* refactor(config): remove unenforced sandbox fields from schema and UI

Greptile correctly flagged that sandbox.network, workspace_mount,
memory_limit, cpu_quota, and trusted_domains were documented and
exposed in the UI but had no runtime effect (apply_to was never
called). This creates a false security promise.

Remove these fields from PresetSandboxPolicy (keeping only mode
which IS enforced via SandboxRouter.set_override), the schema map,
the gateway API response, the UI, docs, and template.

The fields can be re-added when SandboxRouter gains per-session
config overlays for network/workspace/resource policies.

* fix: MCP allow-list enforcement at tool registry level

Two issues from Greptile:

1. TOML merge ordering: raw top-level keys (model, timeout_secs)
   were prepended AFTER generated section headers, misassigning

   then appending generated [mcp]/[sandbox]/[skills] sections.

   loaded from mcp-servers.json registry. Fixed by moving allow-list
   enforcement from the policy deny layer to apply_runtime_tool_filters

   express "deny all MCP except these" due to deny-wins-over-allow
   semantics, so allow-list filtering now happens by inspecting tool

Fix ClawHub skill search results (#1196)

* fix(skills): restore ClawHub search results

ClawHub search now takes long enough that per-result metadata lookups pushed the RPC beyond the UI timeout, making successful searches appear empty. The registry also permits duplicate slugs across publishers.

Use metadata returned by search directly, carry owner-qualified references through detail and install operations, bound external requests, and surface failures in gateway logs, the browser console, an inline alert, and a toast.

* fix(skills): reconcile ClawHub reinstall state

Owner-qualified installs used a new manifest key and directory without removing the previous bare-slug installation. Remove only the controlled legacy path after the replacement archive has been validated.\n\nSearch completions also updated shared UI state regardless of which query was current. Invalidate earlier request generations on input changes and ignore their late responses.

* fix(skills): make ClawHub updates transactional

Persist qualified reinstall state before deleting the legacy directory so a manifest write failure leaves the prior installation usable.\n\nCapture search generations when debounce callbacks are scheduled so an obsolete queued callback cannot reactivate an older query.

* fix(skills): retain retryable cleanup markers

Treat legacy directory deletion as post-commit cleanup rather than install failure. Keep an empty manifest tombstone until cleanup succeeds so retries can reconcile transient filesystem errors without rediscovering the old skill.

* fix(skills): canonicalize bare ClawHub installs

Resolve legacy bare-slug requests to the validated owner returned by ClawHub metadata. Bare and explicit installs now converge on one qualified source key and directory instead of creating duplicate installations.

fix(ios): stabilize GraphQL project generation

Apollo 2.2.0 could prune the generated MoltisAPI namespace, and XcodeGen ran before codegen restored it. The resulting project omitted the namespace source and local iOS validation failed during Swift compilation.\n\nPin Apollo 2.3.0, verify and retry the required namespace output, and regenerate the Xcode project after GraphQL codegen so recovered sources are always included.

fix(skills): point wacrawl install metadata at the openclaw org (#1192)

Installing the `wacrawl` skill's Go fallback fails. Its `requires.install`
entry asks for `github.com/steipete/wacrawl/cmd/wacrawl@latest`, but wacrawl
was renamed into the `openclaw` organization and its `go.mod` now declares
`module github.com/openclaw/wacrawl`. GitHub serves an HTTP redirect for the
old owner, so the URL still opens in a browser and `git clone` still works —
but the Go module resolver compares the declared module path against the
required one and refuses the mismatch:

    go: github.com/steipete/wacrawl/cmd/wacrawl@latest:
        module declares its path as: github.com/openclaw/wacrawl
                but was required as: github.com/steipete/wacrawl

This is the same failure mode as #1189 (gogcli), applied to the skill asset
rather than the sandbox image.

Migrate the other two stale references in the same frontmatter, matching how
the sibling slacrawl skill already reads:

- `homepage` now names the canonical `openclaw/wacrawl` URL instead of relying
  on GitHub's owner redirect.
- The brew formula moves to `openclaw/tap/wacrawl`. `wacrawl.rb` no longer
  exists in `steipete/homebrew-tap`; it lives in `openclaw/homebrew-tap`. The
  old coordinate still resolves today only because that tap's
  `tap_migrations.json` maps `wacrawl` to `openclaw/tap`, so naming the real
  tap directly drops a dependency on a compatibility shim we do not control.

Cover the entry with `wacrawl_install_metadata_uses_openclaw_sources`,
mirroring the existing slacrawl test: assert the literal post-rename homepage,
formula, and module path, plus negative assertions against each pre-rename
value. The module negative is the load-bearing one, since that is the only
field `go install` hard-fails on.

songsee is deliberately untouched: openclaw/songsee's `go.mod` still declares
`module github.com/steipete/songsee`, so its skill asset is correct as written.

fix(vault): normalize recovery phrase before hashing (#1186)

* fix(vault): normalize recovery phrase before hashing

derive_recovery_kek normalizes the recovery phrase (strips dashes,
uppercases) before deriving the KEK, so unsealing works with phrases
typed in lowercase or with dashes. The stored hash, however, was
computed over the raw phrase, so verify_recovery_hash rejected exactly
those forms that unseal_with_recovery accepts.

Hash both at wrap time and in verify_recovery_hash from the same
normalized form (no-op for existing vaults: generated phrases are
already dashless and uppercase). Extend the case-insensitive test to
cover hash verification and update hash_verification to use the
wrap-produced hash as the source of truth.

* fix(vault): preserve legacy recovery hashes

Older vaults stored SHA-256 hashes of generated uppercase recovery phrases with dashes. Normalized-only verification made those persisted hashes fail after upgrade. Keep normalized verification for new hashes while falling back to the raw phrase representation used by existing installations, with a regression test for the legacy format.

The release gate ran `npx playwright test`, which executes all 518 specs

workflow runs `./e2e/run-ci.sh`, which shards the default project across

was green: sessions, agents, and push-worker state accumulated across
specs that CI never runs together, producing failures like a session list
